Duskwood, originally called Brightwood, is a fiefdom of the kingdom of Stormwind located in the southern-central part of Azeroth, south of Elwynn Forest, east of Westfall, west of Deadwind Pass, and north of Stranglethorn Vale. Beneath the everlasting night, which gave Duskwood its current name, the fel magic unleashed by Medivh upon his death has transformed what was once a beautiful part of Elwynn Forest into a land covered in gnarled trees, along with the black fog hanging over the woods.
Duskwood is inhabited by a defiant people who still cling to their holdings in the face of overwhelming adversity. On all sides lurk dangerous creatures, from hideous undead to ferocious Nightbane worgen and overgrown spiders. Ogres moving in have brought up even more problems. To fight against all these threats, the militia of Duskwood, known as the Night Watch, patrolled the main thoroughfare and protected Darkshire, wary of anything moving through the shadows.
The most prominent geographical feature of the region is the Twilight Grove, which contains one of the Great Trees with a portal leading into the Emerald Dream. The woods also feature several abandoned farmsteads, as well as the prominent Raven Hill Cemetery, which holds the graves of many who have known tragic fates and the restless bodies of others, stirred to undeath by necromancy.

I remember bright skies and peaceful woods.|[[Sven Yorgen]][[The Lurking Lich]]}} '''Duskwood''', originally called '''Brightwood''',{{Ref WoWCV1|159}} is a fiefdom of the [[Stormwind (kingdom)|kingdom of Stormwind]] located in the southern-central part of [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth]], south of [[Elwynn Forest]], east of [[Westfall]], west of [[Deadwind Pass]], and north of [[Stranglethorn Vale]]. Beneath the everlasting night,[[:File:Alliance Hero's Call Board.jpg]] which gave Duskwood its current name, the [[fel]] magic unleashed by [[Medivh]] upon his death has transformed what was once a beautiful part of Elwynn Forest into a land covered in gnarled trees, along with the black fog hanging over the woods. Duskwood is inhabited by a defiant people who still cling to their holdings in the face of overwhelming adversity. On all sides lurk dangerous creatures, from hideous [[undead]] to ferocious [[Nightbane pack|Nightbane]] [[worgen]] and overgrown [[spider]]s. [[Ogre]]s moving in have brought up even more problems. To fight against all these threats, the militia of Duskwood, known as the [[Night Watch]], patrolled the main thoroughfare and protected [[Darkshire]], wary of anything moving through the shadows. The most prominent geographical feature of the region is the [[Twilight Grove]], which contains one of the [[Great Tree]]s with a portal leading into the [[Emerald Dream]]. The woods also feature several abandoned farmsteads, as well as the prominent [[Raven Hill Cemetery]], which holds the graves of many who have known tragic fates and the restless bodies of others, stirred to undeath by necromancy. {{OTOC|460|282}} ==History== {{Stub/Lore-section|Brief summary of Cataclysm, Dark Riders comic, and Legion stories.}} ===Early history=== [[File:Twilight Grove.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|The unnamed [[great tree]] in the [[Twilight Grove]].]] 4,500 years before the Dark Portal, [[Fandral Staghelm]] and his followers secretly cut six enchanted branches from the boughs of [[Nordrassil]]. With the branches in hand, they traveled the world to locations where [[saronite]] blooms had sprung to life, including a remote region of the [[Eastern Kingdoms]] that would later be known as Duskwood. The branch quickly took root, and became a new [[great tree]] all its own, acting as a conduit and channeling the powers of the [[Emerald Dream]] into the waking world, strengthening the nearby wildlife and scouring the saronite deposits.{{Ref WoWCV1|124}} Following the fracturing of the [[Arathor|Arathorian Empire]] around 1200 [[BDP]], the disparate human nations flourished throughout the [[Eastern Kingdoms]]; among them the smallest and most isolated of the kingdoms was [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]]. Over the years, it found prosperity through the farmsteads that dotted the surrounding fertile region, and as its population grew, small towns sprang up in the nearby regions, notably in Brightwood.{{Ref WoWCV1|159}} Also known as "Southern Elwynn Forest", the region was the location of two sizable towns called [[Grand Hamlet]] and [[Raven Hill]].''[[Legends Volume 2]]'', ''[[Warrior: Divided]]'' ===During the First War=== Eventually, during the [[First War]], the Warchief Blackhand ordered raiding parties to cut deep into Stormwind's lands, as he wanted to drive the human populace to panic. Entire villages in Westfall fell to the [[Old Horde]]'s control, their inhabitants either killed or forced to flee.{{Ref WoWCV2|124}} Later, the region was cursed when [[Medivh]] died, [[fel]] energy being unleashed by his death, turning the surrounding land into a dangerous, thorny blight. The area would later become known as Duskwood.{{Ref WoWCV2|134}} Long ago, [[Elwynn Forest]] was populated with a group of [[spider]]s that lived peacefully among the woods. However, when the curse fell over Duskwood - turning the once peaceful woodland into a realm of terror - the spiders began to mutate and grow to monstrous proportions. The lurking [[venom spider]]s began hunting their hapless prey in all of the shadowed corners of the land. Possessing both deadly acidic [[venom]] and powerful webbing, these cruel [[beast]]s stalked any foolish wanderers who stray too far into the haunted woods.[[The World of Warcraft Townhall/Beastiary#Venom Spider]] ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} [[File:Duskwood day.jpg|thumb|Duskwood at day.]] Years ago, humans introduced the [[Rat Snake|rat snakes]] into Duskwood to cull the local rat population.[[Rat Snake]] The reason Duskwood now teems with the undead is because of the vile necromancer [[Morbent Fel]].[[The Fate of Morbent Fel]] Many [[wolf|wolves]] fled from Duskwood to [[Elwynn Forest]],[[Marshal McBride's Documents]] (original) scared by the darkness taking over the wood. A night elf by the name of [[Velinde Starsong]] came to the woods carrying the [[Scythe of Elune]]. Hunted by [[Varkas]], Velinde was killed and the Scythe of Elune was lost in [[Roland's Doom]]. The powerful weapon was later found by members of the [[Defias Brotherhood]] excavating the mine, including a skittish man named [[Jitters]]. Jitters picked up the weapon, triggering its effect of summoning. The mine was immediately filled with [[worgen]], who then proceeded to rip the men apart, while [[Jitters]] escaped with the weapon. In his escape, Jitters lost the weapon in the woods and hid in the barn of the [[Yorgen Farmstead]], but the appearance of the scythe attracted the [[Dark Riders]] from [[Deadwind Pass]], who slaughtered [[Sven Yorgen]]'s family in front of Jitters' eyes. Now the people of Duskwood have to fight against the undead but also the worgen, under the threat from the Dark riders in search of the scythe.''[[Jitters' Completed Journal]]'' ===Pre-Cataclysm=== {{Comic-section}} Mere days before the Fall of Gilneas, the Scythe of Elune was liberated from Duskwood.[[Curse of the Worgen Issue 5|''Curse of the Worgen'' issue 5]] It was rediscovered by the worgen around Manor Mistmantle and Roland's Doom, who served the [[Wolf Cult]]. Seeking to clear his name, Mardigan sought out the cult on his own, questioning the Night Watch before seeking the worgen in the woods. He was followed soon after by [[Archmage Karlain|Karlain]], [[Revil Kost]], and [[Ambrose]], who killed the local worgen leader [[Gervase]], saved Mardigan, and claimed the Scythe of Elune.''[[Dark Riders (comic)|Dark Riders]]'' The scythe was given to the night elves, and was taken to [[Ruins of Gilneas|Gilneas]] by [[Valorn Stillbough|Valorn]] days later. ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} [[File:Darkshire.jpg|thumb|[[Darkshire]], formerly known as Grand Hamlet.]] During the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 ADP, a handful of [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneans]] arrived in Duskwood, such as [[Tobias Mistmantle]] who sought the whereabouts of his brother, [[Stalvan Mistmantle|Stalvan]].[[The Legend of Stalvan (quest)]] Meanwhile, [[Oliver Harris]] and his associates settled in [[Raven Hill]] and performed alchemical testing on captured [[Nightbane pack|Nightbane]] [[worgen]],[[A Curse We Cannot Lift]] saving [[Sven Yorgen]] from the mindless state.[[Cry For The Moon]] The [[Defias Brotherhood|Defias]] [[Defias Night Runner|agents]] in [[Addle's Stead]] left after the fall of the organization, and have since been replaced by [[Forlorn Spirit|forlorn]] [[Wraith|wraiths]] in their place. In [[Raven Hill Cemetery]], [[Morbent Fel]] returned as a [[lich]] and held dominion over the undead, until he was defeated once again by adventurers using the [[:Morbent's Bane]].[[Morbent's Bane (quest)]] ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} During the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]] in 32 ADP, the [[Council of Darkshire]] and many [[Night Watch|watchers]] joined the [[Veiled Hand]], seeking the downfall of Stormwind. Led by [[Althea Ebonlocke|Sister Ebonlocke]], the cultists murdered innocent inhabitants of Darkshire under the orders of [[Melris Malagan|The Herald]], in order to organize a [[demon]]ic ritual in [[Stormwind Keep]]. These plans were ultimately thwarted by the Uncrowned, who sent [[Garona Halforcen]] and an [[assassin]] [[adventurer]] to investigate.[[Cloak and Dagger (quest)]][[The Unseen Blade]] Meaning to pass the [[:Scythe of Elune]] to the [[Druid|balance druid]] adventurer, [[Belysra Starbreeze]] and [[Valorn Stillbough]] transported it from [[Darnassus]] to the [[Twilight Grove]] in Duskwood. Its presence was felt not only by the [[Nightbane pack|Nightbane]] [[worgen]], but the [[Dark Riders]] as well, who killed Valorn and stole away the artifact.''[[Its Rightful Place]]'' The scythe was eventually recovered in the [[Karazhan Catacombs]].''[[The Dark Riders (druid)]]'' ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{Bfa-section}} During the [[Fourth War]] in 33 ADP, Duskwood was plagued by a ferocious [[Nightbane pack|Nightbane]] [[worgen]] named [[Bloodeyes]], leading [[Vassandra Stormclaw]] to help [[Oliver Harris]] study the [[worgen curse]] in [[Raven Hill]].[[Bane of the Nightbane]] After rare bloom called [[Elune's Grace (item)|Elune's Grace]] appeared around [[Manor Mistmantle]], a pack of [[Mistfang Howler|Mistfang wolves]] took up residence in the area.[[The Spirit of the Hunter]] ===Terror by Torchlight=== {{novel-section}} After the armistice in 34 ADP, a [[Necromancer (Terror by Torchlight)|unnamed necromancer]] attempted to overwhelm Duskwood and Darkshire with an army of undead, using the power of the corrupted [[:Torch of Holy Flame]]. The artifact, placed by [[Sarah Ladimore]] in front of [[Forlorn Rowe|Morbent Fel's home]], originally served to dispel the dark enchantments in the region and keep the undead docile in [[Raven Hill Cemetery]]. While the advance of the undead was slowed down by the efforts of the [[Night Watch|watchers]], [[Mathias Shaw]] and [[Flynn Fairwind]] managed to defeat the necromancer and purify the holy torch. After Darkshire was saved, Shaw spoke with Ladimore that he would send Stormwind guards as reinforcements after the necromancer hinted that the threat [[War against the Jailer|was not over]].''[[Terror by Torchlight]]'' ===Shadowlands=== {{Sl-section}} During [[Death Rising]] in 35 ADP, the [[Stormwind Army]] and [[Argent Crusade]] were mobilized to protect Duskwood from the returning [[Scourge]].[[Field Reports (Alliance)]] ==Getting there== ;{{Horde}} Horde: From [[Grom'Gol]] in [[Stranglethorn Vale]], follow the main road north across the bridge across the chasm and right into Duskwood. ;{{Alliance}} Alliance: From [[Three Corners]] in the [[Redridge Mountains]], follow the road south across the bridge into Duskwood. From [[Westfall]], by crossing the bridge to the east. Also, by swimming through the river south of Elwynn Forest. ==Geography== There are no dungeons of any kind and no battlegrounds in this area. The Redridge Range lies on the eastern border of this zone, as these mountains stretch from the zone of the [[Redridge Mountains]] to the zone of [[Deadwind Pass]]. ===Maps and subregions=== [[Archaeology]] only *{{RaceIcon|Rat}} [[Black Rat]] *{{RaceIcon|Snake}} [[Rat Snake]] *{{RaceIcon|Spider}} [[Widow Spiderling]] *{{RaceIcon|Chicken}} [[Chicken]] *{{RaceIcon|Spider}} [[Darkwidow]] {{Untameable}} *{{RaceIcon|Spider}} [[Blackfang (battle pet)|Blackfang]] {{Untameable}} *{{RaceIcon|Spider}} [[Webwinder]] {{Untameable}} }} ==Dig sites== {{Digsite Map|zone=Duskwood|digsites= {{Digsite Note|35|73|1|Vul'Gol Fossil Bank}} {{Digsite Note|47|44|2|Twilight Grove Digsite}} }} Duskwood has two [[dig site]]s: # [[Vul'Gol Ogre Mound]]; contains [[Fossil Archaeology Fragment]]s. # [[Twilight Grove]]; contains [[Night Elf Archaeology Fragment]]s. ==Treasure of Duskwood== Duskwood is rather unique with regard to its [[chest|treasure chests]]. In most zones on Azeroth, treasure chests spawn next to or inside buildings or ruins, often in the middle of a camp of hostile mobs and virtually always with at least one mob guarding it. In Duskwood, especially north of the main road that cuts across the zone, treasure chests will spawn randomly in the forest next to trees and often without any hostile mobs near them. Chests also spawn at ruined buildings in [[Brightwood Grove]] and at the remains of a small house near [[Addle's Stead]], generally with only a single hostile beast wandering nearby and it is fairly easy to loot the chests without drawing aggro. For an Alliance character in a level range of mid-to-high 20s, treasure hunting in Duskwood can be a fun and profitable adventure. ==In ''Cataclysm''== {{cata-section}} Duskwood was a level 18 - 30 zone prior to ''Cataclysm'', but returned for levels 20 - 25. Adventurers are sent here following their experience in [[Redridge Mountains]].http://blue.mmo-champion.com/t/25968836776/current-zone-status/ Areas affected:[http://forums.worldofwarcraft.com/thread.html?topicId=19377467311&sid=1 Frejya’s (MVP) Cataclysm Compilation] *[[Beggar's Haunt]] – [[Abercrombie]] is now here, no [[Horde]] presence *The [[Hushed Bank]] – mobs changed to owls and bears; camp of [[Lars]] and [[Sven Yorgen]] taken over by [[Grave Robber]]s *[[Raven Hill]] – flight master, small [[Worgen]] camp established *[[Raven Hill Cemetery]] – [[Abercrombie]] moved closer to [[Darkshire]] *The [[Yorgen Farmstead]] – no humanoids, but new elemental mobs - [[Corpseweed]] *[[Vul'Gol Ogre Mound]] - an NPC named [[Apprentice Fess]] is on the road outside of the area *New [[Hunter]] Pets - Barn Owl ==''Warcraft III'' map== {{WC3-section}} Beasts with green scales inhabit this jungle, making it hard to spot them. The tileset is called "Ashenvale".''Official Blizzard Warcraft 3 multiplayer maps from the game and its expansion.'' ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} Technically part of the Alliance and under Stormwind's protection, its distance from the mighty fortress and its close proximity to more malevolent forces in the south and east make it a realm of horror.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 46 The [[undead]] roaming the woods were said to have appeared after the beginning of the [[Third War]] and to belong to the [[Scourge]]. ==Notes and trivia== *Duskwood was previously described as having entered its current state shortly after the [[Second War]] due to darkness inside the nearby [[Karazhan]]. *A "Flight to Duskwood" ride features in the [[Blizzard World]] map in ''[[Overwatch franchise|Overwatch]]''. ==Gallery== File:WarCraftII-BeyondTheDarkPortal-Humans-Mission01-Alleria'sJourney.png|Southern Elwynn Forest during the [[Invasion of Draenor]].
